primary_claim: Lightweight LoRA fine-tuning teaches open-source LLMs to reliably detect when a concept vector has been injected into their residual stream (activation steering), reaching up to 95.5% detection and 71.2% concept identification on held-out concepts with zero false positives on clean controls, while base (non-fine-tuned) models rarely exceed chance.

effect.metric: steering-injection detection rate and injected-concept identification rate on held-out concepts
effect.value: best model: 95.5% detection, 71.2% concept identification; detection ranges from 95% (Qwen 32B) to 43% (Llama 8B) across the 7 fine-tuned architectures; zero false positives on clean controls

stated_future_work: Develop a general theory of intervention-awareness spanning steering, prefill, probes, and other forms of computational manipulation
Determine what architectural features make some models better steering detectors
Determine what training is needed to produce steering rejection while keeping models fluent
limitations_stated: Detection is architecture-dependent, varying from 95% (Qwen 32B) to 43% (Llama 8B) under the same recipe, for reasons not yet understood
Detection fails on vector families geometrically orthogonal to the training distribution (e.g. PCA, ICA extracted vectors), creating evasion strategies
Adapter training can degrade factual performance and safety behaviour, though scaling down the adapter mitigates this
quote: The best model reaches 95.5% detection on held-out concepts and 71.2% concept identification.
